messages:
Alex: quick proposal — compact telemetry event rows by normalizing route/tags into a small tag table and storing tag_id references on each event. goal: reduce per-event payload and storage, improve cache locality. high-level tradeoffs: join cost vs storage and network. Thoughts?

Maria: sounds promising. main questions: backfill complexity, read compatibility for console dashboards, and cardinality of tags (how many tag rows per tenant/route).

Jordan: if we go tag_table + tag_id refs we can keep event rows narrow. joins are expensive at petabyte scale though. Suggest a hybrid: tag_id for lookups + periodically maintain denormalized aggregates for dashboards.

Sam: another route — keep JSON blobs but switch to columnar compression (snappy/LZ4) at write-time and pack multiple events into a block. cheaper dev lift, still helps storage, but ad-hoc queries need decompression.

Alex: benchmark notes: current avg event ~1.2KB; tag portion ~400B. Normalization could save ~50-65% on event storage for high-cardinality tenants. Backfill estimate: 12–18 node-hours per 30 days of data (ballpark), depending on parallelism. Proposal: shadow-write schema v2 (tag refs) for 2 weeks, validate, then backfill a rolling 30-day window.

Liv: console impact: UI expects route metadata inline. We should add a query shim / view that materializes route fields so dashboards aren't blocked. Frontend migration should be opt-in per dashboard.

Jordan: DDL thought: create event_tag_map (event_id, tag_id) plus tag table (tag_id, tenant_id, key, value, created_at). For fast filtering we need an index on (tag_id, timestamp) or a route_tag inverted mapping. That will be read-fast but write-heavy.

Sam: note: adding secondary index increases write amplification ~15-25% and adds storage overhead. But queries that filter by tag+time will go from slow scan to indexed seek. We should quantify based on top-100 dashboard queries.

Alex: rollout steps I'm proposing:
1) create tag table (immutable ids) + event_tag_map DDL (no GC)
2) enable shadow-write in ingest pipeline (write both formats)
3) implement read-view in query layer that unions old rows + normalized mapping (feature-flagged)
4) migrate top dashboards and alerting to new view, validate counts and latencies
5) run backfill for X days and compare results
6) flip reads and schedule GC for legacy fields after safety window

Maria: that looks sane. please add expected metrics to validate (per-tenant avg row size, query p95 for top dashboards, index write amplification, storage delta). Also update runbook with rollback steps.

Jordan: technical ask: when shadow-writing, keep a deterministic tag_id generation (hash + namespace) so backfills are idempotent. Avoid auto-increment to make cross-cluster merges easier.

Sam: will model write qps impact and give numbers. I'll also run a throughput test with synthetic tag cardinality (low/med/high) to show index costs.

IngestBot: shadow-write enabled on prod ingest pipeline for schema_v2 at 1991234580 (note: can be toggled via /ingest toggle-shadow schema_v2).

Alex: action items: Jordan prototype tag_index DDL + perf test; Sam estimate backfill node-hours + write amp; Liv inventory dashboards likely affected; Maria draft rollout doc + validation metrics. I'll set a sync Thu 10am.

Liv: one more ops gotcha — compaction/retention job needs to be aware of compressed blocks vs normalized rows. otherwise GC/compaction may inflate temporary storage. add to runbook.

Maria: :thumbsup: adding compaction note and will update the playbook with rollback and monitoring queries (count diffs, ingest lag, p95 query time).

Jordan: following up — I'll post DDL + simple perf numbers in the thread by EOD tomorrow.

Alex: awesome. thanks everyone.
